> Default GPIO value. Only used if the first attempt to read the GPIO fails.

Done
We should probably add a check here that if Default was specified, then Direction is Input. It should not be valid to have a default value for an Output GPIO. Please add a test for that too.
Done

Can we change this to getDefaultValue()?

Then it will make more sense in combination with the other get value methods:
* getValue()
* getPreviousValue()
* getDefaultValue()

I think we should default all the chassis to missing (ie 1), per story 5026.

Since the gpios can be configured with the polarity, would it make sense to keep this as 0? As the reset of the code would be able to treat 0 as missing and 1 as present not seeing what happens in the background in gpio.
Ah I see, yep I agree.  We'll use the default not as a default of the hw, but from the perspective of the gpio fw name.  Strike my comment from the record please.

no change

These are actually active high.  The hardware is implemented as "prevent_pulse_n", which means set the gpio to 0 to PREVENT the bmc reset.  The fw naming convention is "reset-ENABLE" - in other words, set to 1 to enable the bmc reset, set to 0 to prevent the bmc reset.

Done
Changed all EnableSystemResetGpio's to High.
thanks

The parser code and the Huygens.json file both still use the property name "Default" rather than "DefaultValue". So there is a mismatch between the doc and the code/json.

I think DefaultValue is more descriptive, but Default is nice and short. Either is fine with me. But the doc/code/json need to all match.
